description: Golden fixtures (Paket 8, Phase B) for Filter and Remove, shared by the Rust engine (cargo test, src-tauri/src/text_processor.rs) and the JS engine (npm test, tests/unit/filter-remove.test.ts). They characterize the CURRENT behaviour: a passing test means the behaviour is described correctly, not that it is wanted. Every case states all options explicitly (no defaults). 'pattern' is a string or { repeat, count } (the string repeated count times). Filter expectations: the result text or { error: invalidRegex | regexRuntime | invalidMode | patternEmpty | patternTooLong } (invalidMode, Paket 8 C3: an unknown or empty mode, checked before anything else; patternEmpty / patternTooLong, Paket 10 C3 E3: an empty regex pattern or one of more than 10000 UTF-16 code units, refused by both engines after the mode and before compiling; a plain Remove search term and the duplicates mode are not checked); JS only: { error: regexSplitsCharacter } (Paket 8 C1: a JS match would cut a surrogate pair apart, the worker refuses instead of returning damaged text). Remove expectations: { text, removedLines } or { error }. A case with different engine results uses expectedRust + expectedJs and a divergence { kind, reason }; kinds: dialect (accepted regex dialect difference, Paket 5), utf16Guard (Rust processes valid Unicode, JS refuses a result that would contain cut characters; required for regexSplitsCharacter), suspectedBug, inconsistentDefinition, unvalidatedInput. Every successful JS result must be well-formed Unicode. 'ref' points to the Phase A report (docs/analyse/Paket8-PhaseA-Filter-Remove-Analyse.md). 'openQuestion' marks identical behaviour that still needs a product decision. 'resolved' explains why an expectation was changed by a correction (e.g. Paket 8 C2: in remove mode only a line from which a match removed text and whose rest is blank is dropped; lines without removed text stay unchanged). 'expectedJsUnreachableMainThread' characterizes FilterService.frontendInMainThread, which invoke never reaches (not a product path). Paket 10 Phase B (docs/analyse/Paket10-PhaseB-Regexvertrag.md; 'ref' R1..R10 = docs/analyse/Paket10-PhaseA-Regex-Analyse.md): 'target' is the result of a not yet implemented decision in both engines, always with 'pending' { decisions, phase, engines, reason }: exactly the engines listed in 'engines' still differ from the target (checked against the real engines). Filter only: 'preview' { segments, keepSplitCutsCharacter?, target?, pending?, note?, resolved? } is the pattern preview of the Filter page (JS MatchPreviewWorker with caseSensitive and splitMatches, no mode): 'segments' are its CURRENT rows [text, match, ..., text] per line with a non-empty highlight, or { error: invalidRegex | patternEmpty | patternTooLong | regexSplitsCharacter }; Paket 10 C2 (E1): a match that cuts a character in every Filter mode is the error regexSplitsCharacter, adjacent matches joined at a surrogate pair are one highlight and, with splitMatches, 'keepSplitCutsCharacter': true (only keep with split matches refuses them); 'resolved' explains a changed preview expectation; 'target' + 'pending' { decisions, phase, reason } is a still open preview decision; no row contains a lone surrogate, every row rebuilds its input line, and the preview judgement together with the mode of the case gives the JS Filter verdict. The preview shows matches, not the Filter result (E2): 'note' explains a difference.
